items.title: New York and California Age Gating Rules Go Into Effect in the New Year
items.summary: Come January 2027, everyday social media browsing in two of the country's largest states will look noticeably different. In California, AB 1709 (2026), AB 1043 (2025), and SB 976 (2024) are slated to take effect on January 1, 2027. Meanwhile, state attorney general regulations for New York’s Stop Addictive Feeds Exploitation (SAFE) for Kids Act take effect on January 25, 2027. EFF has opposed these laws across legislatures , regulatory proceedings , and the courts . The core problem is simple: age-gating mandates trade away everyday user privacy and free expression under the guise of safety, while pushing platforms to gather even more personal data on users. What California’s Rules Say Three interlocking California laws take effect on January 1, 2027, reshaping how platforms handle age checks and design features for young users. First, SB 976 (2024) requires verifiable parental consent before platforms can offer algorithmic feeds or nighttime notifications to anyone under 18. items.title: Department of Justice Announces Awarding of Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies
items.summary: NEW ORLEANS — Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office), the Department of Justice today announced it has awarded nearly $150 million under the 2026 COPS Hiring Program (CHP). CHP is a competitive grant program that provides funding directly to state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to pay for the entry-level salaries and fringe benefits of newly hired and rehired full-time sworn officers/deputies to make America safe again.  In the Eastern District of Louisiana (4) municipalities were awarded funding totaling more than 7 million dollars.

items.title: U.S. Attorney for Northern Ohio Announces Contribution to Protecting Americans from Fraud in Largest-Ever Crackdown on Scammers
items.summary: United States Attorney David M. Toepfer joined Attorney General Todd Blanche and other law enforcement officials in announcing decisive action against foreign and domestic scams. The Justice Department’s historic surge in resources to protect Americans from criminal scam networks and online fraud follows President Trump’s Executive Order 14390 directing a government-wide crackdown.

items.title: District Court Orders Queens-Based Logistics Company, Affiliate, and Their Owner to Pay $300,000 and Cease Sending Packages Through United States Mail
items.summary: Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and Darnell Edwards, Acting Inspector in Charge, United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) announced today a settlement agreement with Yizhao Hou and two companies he controls, YDH Express Inc. and YDH Int’l Inc. (together, Defendants).  The settlement, so ordered by the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York on November 25, 2026, resolves the lawsuit filed by the United States against Defendants in May 2025, alleging that Defendants violated the False Claims Act (FCA) by shipping thousands of parcels bearing counterfeit United States Postal Service (USPS) labels that Defendants received from their customers in China and seeking injunctive relief pursuant to the Anti-Fraud Injunction Act.  Defendants will pay $300,000 and agree to permanently cease using USPS to mail parcels.

items.title: Mexican National Indicted for Reentry of a Removed Alien
items.summary: NEW ORLEANS, LA –  In a recently unsealed indictment, JORGE LUIS CISNEROS-ZUNIGA (“CISNEROS-ZUNIGA”) , 52, a native of Mexico, was indicted on November 13, 2026, for reentry of a removed alien, in violation of Title 8, United States Code, Section 1326(a) and (b)(1), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.
